client.name: Saffron Lane Supper Club
client.about: Saffron Lane Supper Club is a group of neighbors who cook together every Thursday in the kitchen of a community center. RecipeBox is their shared cookbook: what they cooked, how much of each thing, and what everyone thought of it. They read it on a phone propped against a jar, with flour on their hands.
client.contacts: Bianca Moretti (club organizer), Leo Tanaka (volunteer cook) and Ingrid Solberg (who keeps the site running) report the tickets.

project.name: RecipeBox
project.about: A cookbook shared by a few cooks: recipes with ingredients and steps, quantities that follow the number of servings, a search by text and by ingredient, ratings and favorites. Its data lives in a PostgreSQL database.
project.stack: React, Vite, TanStack Query, React Hook Form and Tailwind; Node.js, Fastify and Sequelize; PostgreSQL

welcome.subject: Welcome to the RecipeBox project!
welcome.body:
Hi, and welcome aboard!

I'm Rafaela, the engineering manager here. You're joining **RecipeBox**, the shared cookbook we build for the **Saffron Lane Supper Club**, a group of neighbors who cook together every Thursday. They open it in the kitchen, in the middle of a recipe, so when something is wrong they find out with a pan on the stove.

Here's how we work:

- Your tickets show up on the **Board**. Take one at a time: drag it to **In Progress** when you start, and to **In QA** when you think it's done. Most tickets are bugs to fix; one asks you to build something that is missing, and one to finish something that was left half done.
- The code lives in your workspace container. **Open in VS Code** attaches your editor to it, with Node, the terminal and the debugger already set up. Run `npm run dev` in the VS Code terminal and use **Open app in browser** to try the cookbook.
- This project has a real database server: a **PostgreSQL** that runs next to your workspace. The Dashboard shows whether it is ready. To look inside, run `psql "$DATABASE_URL"` in the VS Code terminal, and `npm run db:reset` puts the sample cookbook back whenever you want a clean start.
- The server is built with Fastify and talks to the database through Sequelize; the form of the page uses React Hook Form. If any of them is new to you, read `README.md` first: it says where each kind of code lives.
- QA runs the project tests first, then checks the ticket itself. If something fails, the card comes back with notes.
- Stuck? Message **Priya** from the ticket. She'll point you in the right direction, one hint at a time.

When you're ready, click **Get next assignment**. I picked a nice first one for you.

Rafaela

back-1.subject: New ticket: RB-201
back-1.body:
A recipe saved with the time "1h30" cannot be saved again from its edit form: the API refuses the same text it accepted when the recipe was created.

Compare the two requests side by side.

Rafaela

back-2.subject: New ticket: RB-202
back-2.body:
Pressing + on a recipe for 4 gives 41 servings and two kilos of flour. The page only adds one to what the server sends.

Follow the number backwards, from the page to where it is stored.

Rafaela

back-3.subject: New ticket: RB-203
back-3.body:
Ingrid's clean-up script deleted a recipe that does not exist and was told it worked. The API answers a success for a delete that did nothing.

A short one, and a good look at how the API answers.

Rafaela

back-4.subject: New ticket: RB-204
back-4.body:
The search cannot find the club's most cooked recipe. Bianca noticed the pattern: only recipes with a photo are ever found.

The search is one query in the server. Read what the ORM does with it.

Rafaela

back-5.subject: New ticket: RB-205
back-5.body:
Choosing a category and typing an ingredient gives recipes of every category. Each filter works alone; together, one of them wins.

Look at the place where the filters meet.

Rafaela

back-6.subject: New ticket: RB-206
back-6.body:
Fixing a typo in a published recipe turns it back into a draft and deletes its ratings for good. Members have stopped correcting recipes.

The ticket has the rules of the cookbook. Check what an edit writes against them.

Rafaela

back-7.subject: New ticket: RB-207
back-7.body:
This one is not a bug. Someone replaced the steps of a recipe and nobody can tell who: the log of the server does not say. Ingrid wants one line per change, with the cook.

The ticket says exactly what the line must have, and what it must not.

Rafaela

back-8.subject: New ticket: RB-208
back-8.body:
This one is unfinished work. Favorites work in the list; on the recipe page the heart is always empty, and "Only favorites" fails. The server side was left half done, with notes in the code.

Read what is there before you add to it.

Rafaela

front-1.subject: New ticket: RB-101
front-1.body:
Leo took the butter out of a recipe, saved, and the butter was back. The row leaves the form and returns in the saved recipe.

Start by looking at what the page actually sends when the form is saved.

Rafaela

front-2.subject: New ticket: RB-102
front-2.body:
The cookbook has recipes with no ingredients at all. The form has a rule against that, with a message written and everything, and the rule never fires.

The form is built with React Hook Form. Read what the rule really means before changing it.

Rafaela

front-3.subject: New ticket: RB-103
front-3.body:
Bianca searches the cookbook, opens a recipe, comes back, and her search is gone. She also cannot send anyone a link to a search.

Think about where the filters of the list should live.

Rafaela

front-4.subject: New ticket: RB-104
front-4.body:
After a recipe is edited, the list keeps showing the old one until the page is reloaded. Two members saved the same change twice because of it.

The server is fine. Look at what the page keeps and when it lets go of it.

Rafaela

front-5.subject: New ticket: RB-105
front-5.body:
An old link to a deleted recipe opens an empty recipe, with the Publish and Delete buttons on it. A member thought she had broken something.

The server answers 404 correctly. Find out why the page does not notice.

Rafaela

front-6.subject: New ticket: RB-106
front-6.body:
The club cooks with a phone propped on the counter, and on a phone the steps of every recipe are cut off on the right. They are guessing oven temperatures.

It is a small change once you see it. Use the device toolbar of the developer tools.

Rafaela

front-7.subject: New ticket: RB-107
front-7.body:
A member who uses only the keyboard cannot rate recipes: the stars never get the focus, and her screen reader does not mention them.

This one matters to Bianca. Try the page yourself without the mouse first.

Rafaela

front-8.subject: New ticket: RB-108
front-8.body:
When a cook changes the number of servings, the whole ingredient list becomes the first ingredient, repeated. With the recipe's own servings it looks right.

Read the component slowly. It is a short one.

Rafaela

completion.subject: RecipeBox: project done!
completion.body:
You completed the whole {{track}} track of RecipeBox, so this project is done on your side. Bianca says last Thursday was the first club night without anyone shouting a question across the kitchen about the cookbook, and Leo and Ingrid send their thanks too.

You can keep going with the other tracks of RecipeBox whenever you like. New projects are on their way too.

Thanks for the effort.

Rafaela

trackCompletion.subject: The {{track}} track is done!
trackCompletion.body:
You closed every {{track}} ticket of RecipeBox. Bianca noticed: members are fixing and rating recipes again.

Thanks for the effort.

Rafaela
